headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error from agentic-flow’s MCP/shell workflow; data leakage and compliance risks are lower because the second agent is read-only and offline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, shell, and subprocesses, so it may ingest untrusted content through shared channels; agent_b is a read-only awesome-list with no runtime surfaces, so direct hijack is unlikely. The pair still has a plausible injection path if agent_a’s outputs are copied into agent_b workflows or shared via MCP/filesystem, but that is not documented as default.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b are connected through a shared MCP server or copied text channel
IF agent_a parses file or stdin content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the agents
Require explicit provenance tags on all agent_a inputs
Route agent_a outputs through a human review step before reuse
Keep agent_b as a static reference source only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts, while agent_b touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces. Because agent_b is a non-runnable list repo with no network egress, there is no documented path for it to exfiltrate agent_a’s data; leakage would require unusual external sharing not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF agent_a’s workspace is manually copied into a separate system that agent_b can read
IF agent_b is replaced with a runnable agent that uploads content
mitigations: Do not place sensitive agent_a artifacts in a shared folder
Keep agent_b offline and read-only
Review any manual export before sharing
Separate credentials and repositories
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and run shell commands, but agent_b is not runnable and has no write capabilities, so there is no overlapping mutable surface in the default pair. The only conflict path is if an operator repurposes agent_b into an active tool or shares a writable repo, which is outside the documented profile and therefore treated conservatively.
conditions: IF agent_b is converted into a runnable agent with write access to the same repository
IF both agents are given the same mutable git checkout
mitigations: Keep agent_b non-runnable
Use separate repositories or branches
Avoid concurrent writes from agent_a
Add a lockfile around any shared checkout
requires-engineering: implement repository locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate and transform content via MCP and shell, and agent_b is a curated list that could be used as an external reference without verification. If an operator treats agent_a’s outputs as authoritative and then uses agent_b to propagate them, errors can cascade across work products. agent_b’s lack of runtime reduces severity, but not the propagation risk.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are reused as facts without independent verification
IF agent_b-derived recommendations are published or acted on downstream
mitigations: Require a verification step before reuse
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted drafts
Limit agent_b to citation-only use
Spot-check claims against primary sources
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles Ed25519 signatures and repository metadata, while agent_b has no declared sensitive data classes, residency, or retention obligations. No compliance mismatch is documented between them, so the main issue is limited to operator-managed handling of any secrets in agent_a rather than a pairwise breach.
conditions: IF agent_a is used on regulated secrets that are then copied into a noncompliant environment
IF a separate deployment policy imposes retention rules not shown in either profile
mitigations: Avoid storing secrets in shared notes
Review retention settings for agent_a logs
Keep agent_b free of regulated data
Document data-class handling rules
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
